Answers.content:
The dot product of two vectors \(\mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \\ a_3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \\ b_3 \end{pmatrix}\) is defined as:

\[
\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + a_3b_3
\]

In the context of the given vectors \(\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 0 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\), the dot product is calculated as:

\[
(-2)(3) + (0)(4) + (7)(-5) = -6 + 0 - 35 = -41
\]

While this definition can be assumed in most mathematical contexts, it is generally good practice to explicitly state the formula or definition being used, especially when presenting a calculation for clarity and completeness.
